message.content:
In Blackjack an **Ace can count as either 1 or 11**, whichever is more advantageous to the hand.  
- **If counting it as 11 keeps the hand ≤ 21**, the Ace is treated as 11.  
- **If counting it as 11 would bust the hand**, the Ace automatically “drops” to 1.  

This flexibility means:
- A hand of Ace + 10‑value card (10, J, Q, K) is a *natural* 21 (blackjack).  
- With two Aces, one is usually counted as 11 and the other as 1 (so the hand is 12).  
- If you’re dealt an Ace and a 9, you can hit for a 10 to make 20, or you can stand on 20.  
- If you’re dealt an Ace and a 7, you can hit for a 10 to make 18, or you can stand on 18.  

The rule is the same in all standard casino Blackjack variations: the Ace is flexible, but you can never count it as both 1 and 11 at the same time.
